title: Sibol Honor of Kings bags Bronze Medal at Asian Games 2026

blocks.text: Sibol’s Honor of Kings squad came into the Asian Games with a podium finish as its target. It left Aichi-Nagoya with a bronze medal after making its way through a long opening day, sweeping South Korea in the quarterfinals, and eventually falling to defending champion China in the semifinals.

The Philippines began its Honor of Kings campaign in Pool B, where it opened with a 2-0 sweep of Kazakhstan. Sibol then faced Malaysia in its second match of the day, losing the series to finish second in the group. That was enough to send the team into the knockout stage, where it drew South Korea.

The quarterfinal against South Korea became the turning point of the run. Sibol controlled both games and completed another 2-0 sweep, securing a place in the semifinals and, with it, at least a bronze medal. The result also gave the Philippines its second esports medal of the Asian Games, coming less than an hour after Sibol’s Pokémon UNITE team had also secured bronze.

Head coach Gerald ‘Tgee’ Gelacio credited the team’s clean play after the South Korea series, pointing to the limited number of mistakes the squad made throughout the match. The players knew, however, that the harder part of the bracket was still ahead. China, the reigning Honor of Kings Asian Games champion, was waiting in the semifinals.

Sibol had little time to prepare. After playing its pool matches and quarterfinal on the same day, the team spent its remaining time studying China and preparing for the semifinal. Justine ‘Juschie’Tan said the team wanted to stick to its own game rather than get overwhelmed by the occasion or its opponent.

China ultimately ended the Philippines’ run in the semifinals, sending Sibol to the bronze-medal position. China advanced to the gold-medal match against Malaysia, while the Philippines collected its second esports bronze of the 2026 Asian Games.

For Sibol’s Honor of Kings lineup, the medal capped a run that started with a pool-stage split and became more convincing as the knockout rounds arrived. The team swept Kazakhstan, fell to Malaysia, swept South Korea when a medal was on the line, and then pushed its run as far as the semifinals before China stopped it.
The Philippines did not make the final, but the Honor of Kings team still leaves Aichi-Nagoya with a medal from its first Asian Games campaign in the title as an already impressive feat.
